issue.title: aws_savingsplans_savings_plan: Create fails/hangs and never persists to state for No Upfront plans and future purchase_time
issue.body:
### Terraform and AWS Provider Version

```console
Terraform and AWS Provider Version
  Terraform v1.15.8
  on darwin_arm64
  + provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws v6.57.1
```

### Affected Resource(s) or Data Source(s)


  aws_savingsplans_savings_plan

### Expected Behavior

1. Creating a No Upfront Savings Plan (e.g. Database plan type, which only offers No Upfront) should succeed without a schema-consistency error.
2. Setting purchase_time to a future date should schedule (queued) the purchase and either return control to the user promptly, or at minimum not silently strand a real, billed purchase outside of Terraform state if the wait is interrupted or times out.

### Actual Behavior

Issue 1 -- inconsistent result on No Upfront plans:

terraform apply calls CreateSavingsPlan successfully (the plan is actually purchased and billed in AWS), then fails Terraform's own post-apply consistency check because upfront_payment_amount is not marked Computed in the schema. Omitting it plans as a concrete null, but AWS returns a real value ("0.00000000") for a No Upfront plan, failing the check. Explicitly setting upfront_payment_amount = "0.00000000" as a workaround is also rejected -- this time by the AWS API itself (ValidationException: Upfront payment for No Upfront Savings Plans cannot be provided and automatically defaults to 0).

So there is no valid configuration that successfully creates a No Upfront Savings Plan: omit the argument -> provider consistency error; set it -> AWS API validation error.

A related, smaller version of the same defect: commitment is also not marked Computed, and AWS returns it padded to 8 decimal places (e.g. "30.00000000") regardless of input precision, causing a similar inconsistency/taint unless the caller pre-formats input to match exactly.

Issue 2 -- future purchase_time causes an unbounded hang and an unrecoverable state gap:

When purchase_time is a future date, the plan correctly enters queued state in AWS immediately. However, the resource's Create waiter treats queued as pending, not terminal (Pending: [PaymentPending, Queued], Target: [Active]). So apply blocks ("Still creating...") until the plan actually transitions to active, which may be hours or days away. The default create timeout (30m) is reliably exceeded for any scheduled purchase.

resp.State.Set() is only called after the waiter returns successfully -- there is no intermediate state write once CreateSavingsPlan itself succeeds. So on timeout: the real purchase has already happened and is being billed in AWS, but Terraform has no record of it in state. A user who retries apply without first running terraform import will trigger a second, duplicate CreateSavingsPlan call -- a real financial mistake, not just a cosmetic plan error.

### Relevant Error/Panic Output

│ Error: Provider produced inconsistent result after apply
│
│ When applying changes to aws_savingsplans_savings_plan.this, provider
│ "registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws" produced an unexpected new value:
│ .upfront_payment_amount: was null, but now cty.StringVal("0.00000000").
│
│ This is a bug in the provider, which should be reported in the provider's
│ own issue tracker.
╵

--- separately, when upfront_payment_amount is set explicitly: ---

╷
│ Error: creating Savings Plans Savings Plan
│
│ Cause: operation error savingsplans: CreateSavingsPlan, ValidationException:
│ Upfront payment for No Upfront Savings Plans cannot be provided and
│ automatically defaults to 0.
╵

### Sample Terraform Configuration

hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "~> 6.57.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  region = "us-east-1"
}

data "aws_savingsplans_offerings" "this" {
  plan_types      = ["Database"]
  payment_options = ["No Upfront"]
  durations       = [31536000] # 1 year
  currencies      = ["USD"]
}

resource "aws_savingsplans_savings_plan" "this" {
  savings_plan_offering_id = data.aws_savingsplans_offerings.this.offerings[0].offering_id
  commitment                = "30.00000000"

  # Issue 2 reproduction: set a future purchase_time, e.g.
  # purchase_time = "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"
}

Steps to Reproduce
1. terraform init
2. terraform apply
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  region = "us-east-1"
}

data "aws_savingsplans_offerings" "this" {
  plan_types      = ["Database"]
  payment_options = ["No Upfront"]
  durations       = [31536000] # 1 year
  currencies      = ["USD"]
}

resource "aws_savingsplans_savings_plan" "this" {
  savings_plan_offering_id =data.aws_savingsplans_offerings.this.offerings[0].offering_id
  commitment                = "30.00000000"

  # Issue 2 reproduction: set a future purchase_time, e.g.
  # purchase_time = "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"
}


### Steps to Reproduce

1. terraform init
2. terraform apply

### Debug Logging

Not captured with TF_LOG=trace for this report; the error above was reproduced from a standard terraform apply run. Happy to capture full debug output on request.


### GenAI / LLM Assisted Development

Claude Code

### Important Facts and References

 Database Savings Plans only offer the no upfront payment option - this is no alternative payment option to route issue 1 for this plan type.
Both issues share a root cause: does not persist any state until after its waiter reached the active target state.
the real financial purchase suceeds via the AWS API in both cases.

### Would you like to implement a fix?

No
